import csv

# Generate the first 12 Fibonacci numbers
fibonacci = []
a, b = 0, 1
for i in range(12):
    fibonacci.append(a)
    a, b = b, a + b

# Write to CSV file
with open('/tmp/fibonacci.csv', 'w', newline='') as csvfile:
    writer = csv.writer(csvfile)
    writer.writerow(['Index', 'Fibonacci Number'])
    for i, num in enumerate(fibonacci, 1):
        writer.writerow([i, num])

print("First 12 Fibonacci numbers:")
for i, num in enumerate(fibonacci, 1):
    print(f"{i}: {num}")

print("\nCSV file created at /tmp/fibonacci.csv")

content.text:
**Reykjavík (the city proper/municipality) has a population of approximately 139,000–140,000 as of early 2025–2026 estimates, while the Greater Reykjavík / Capital Region (metropolitan area) has about 253,230 residents as of the end of Q2 2026.**[[1]](https://www.statice.is/publications/news-archive/inhabitants/population-in-the-2nd-quarter-2026/)[[2]](https://www.icelandreview.com/news/iceland-population-grows-second-quarter-2026/)

Official data from Statistics Iceland (the primary source) reports:
- Capital Region population: 253,230 (end of June 2026).[[1]](https://www.statice.is/publications/news-archive/inhabitants/population-in-the-2nd-quarter-2026/)
- Reykjavík municipality: 138,772 (as of 1 January 2025).[[3]](https://www.statice.is/publications/news-archive/inhabitants/population-in-reykjavik-by-districts-2025)

Other sources, such as World Population Review, estimate Reykjavík at 249,228 for 2026 (likely referring to the urban/metro area) and note steady growth.[[4]](https://worldpopulationreview.com/cities/iceland/reykjavik)

Note that figures vary slightly depending on whether "Reykjavík" refers to the municipality/urban settlement or the broader Capital Region (which includes surrounding municipalities like Kópavogur and Hafnarfjörður and accounts for roughly 64% of Iceland’s total population of ~396,500). Official Statistics Iceland data is the most authoritative for recent quarterly figures.
